Table of a correlation matrix (lower triangle), same layout as the heatmap

Source: R/tables.R
tbl_cor_matrix.Rd

Table of a correlation matrix (lower triangle), same layout as the heatmap

Usage

tbl_cor_matrix(
  cm,
  labels = NULL,
  use_adj = TRUE,
  order = c("original", "hclust"),
  digits = 2,
  palette = COR_PAL,
  bin_mark = " [0/1]",
  title = NULL,
  subtitle = NULL
)

Arguments

cm

output of cor_test_matrix()

labels

named vector variable -> label

use_adj

stars on adjusted (TRUE) or raw p-values

order

"original" or "hclust" (same ordering as plot_cor_heatmap())

digits

decimals

palette

colours (named low / high); NULL = no colour

bin_mark

marker of binary variables

title, subtitle

override the automatic texts

Value

a gt_tbl

Examples

d  <- simulate_cor_data(150)
cm <- cor_test_matrix(d, c("CRP", "IL6", "BDNF", "NfL", "BIN_CRP"))
tbl_cor_matrix(cm, labels = attr(d, "labels"))

1 Binary variable [0/1], coded 0/1 (upper level = 1).
    
Adjusted p, Benjamini-Hochberg (FDR) over the 10 distinct pairs: * < 0.05, ** < 0.01, *** < 0.001; no star = adjusted p ≥ 0.05.
    
Continuous: r_s = cov(rank_x, rank_y) / (SD(rank_x) × SD(rank_y)); t-test, n − 2 df.
    
Binary [0/1]: r_s = r_rb × √(3pq), r_rb = 2 AUC − 1 (rank-biserial, ≡ Mann-Whitney test), p, q = group proportions; |r_s| ≤ 0.87, not comparable with continuous pairs.
    
Notation: Makowski D, Ben-Shachar MS, Patil I, Lüdecke D (2020), J Open Source Softw 5(51):2306, doi:10.21105/joss.02306.
